operation: velocity-space perturbation and k -> electric field
discovery.model: Linear one-dimensional single-spatial-Fourier-mode electrons, fixed ions.
discovery.geometry: One velocity coordinate and one spatial Fourier mode.
discovery.boundary: One Fourier mode; linear discrete Poisson closure; no time advance.

identity.model: Linear one-dimensional single-spatial-Fourier-mode electrons, fixed ions.
identity.geometry: One velocity coordinate and one spatial Fourier mode.
identity.boundary: One Fourier mode; linear discrete Poisson closure; no time advance.
assumptions: Velocity-window truncation and recurrence are separate from temporal integration error.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: Complex scalar electric field satisfying ikE=-dv sum(df). Returns the computed value positionally: the caller receives it directly, not as a field of a returned mapping.
outputs.shape: As described in output mapping or tuple.
outputs.constraints: Finite complex scalar equal to the discrete Poisson field.

preconditions: df is a finite one-dimensional vector with at least two entries.
k is finite and nonzero; dv is finite and positive.
excluded: Nonlinear fields, multidimensional modes and k=0.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: ValueError for non-vector/nonfinite df, nonfinite or zero k, or nonpositive/nonfinite dv.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: FloatingPointError when the computed field is not finite.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; this is a direct algebraic closure.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No field is returned after an exception.

example.code:
from scirel.kinetic.vlasov_poisson import vp_field
assert vp_field([1,2],.5,.1) == .6000000000000001j
example.description: Evaluate the discrete Poisson closure for df=[1,2], k=0.5 and dv=0.1.

scope: Independent reference: exact rational arithmetic. Every input is an exact binary rational, so (i/k) dv sum(df) is recomputed with fractions.Fraction and rounds only at the final conversion; the same comparison is then run with a flipped sign and with a doubled dv to show that both exceed the budget, so the budget cannot admit an arbitrary value.

Implementation relation: the field is the correction field (i/k) dv sum(df), i.e. the discrete statement i k E = -dv sum(df); k must be finite and nonzero and dv positive and finite; the field is a scalar, not an array, and is not an external or total field.

Test matrix: three configurations including negative k and the pair k = 12 with dv = 1e-3 that exercises the scale; a non-vector input; k = 0; a negative dv; and an overflowing sum that must raise FloatingPointError rather than return infinity.
Precision budget, declared before the comparison was run: 8 eps |E|, which is one rounding of an otherwise exact rational calculation, with the sign and dv discrimination asserted separately.
Evidence ceiling: the closure is a discrete Fourier projection at a single k. Nothing here establishes its continuum limit, and the neutral k = 0 mode is rejected rather than handled.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Independent semidiscrete mathematical and selected scenario regressions; actual run/installed-wheel receipts are recorded separately, not inferred from test existence.
known_limitations: Finite-window rectangle rule and sampling recurrence TR=2pi/(k*dv).
Fn4 truncated density retains original coefficient and is not renormalized after cutoff.
Peak diagnostic assumes standing oscillation; rotating complex exponential has no amplitude peaks.

basis.statement: Independent semidiscrete mathematical checks and selected scenario regressions in the bound file. Actual run/installed-wheel receipts are recorded separately and are NOT inferred from test existence.
